name: Shintani Shuzo
about: Shintani Shuzo makes sake in Tokuji, a town of about 6,000 people in Yamaguchi, and sells it as Wakamusume. Shintani Kumakichi founded it in 1927, after working in a local brewery and then buying one that had stopped brewing. The town once had five or more breweries, and this is the last one.

Since 2007 it has run as a four-season brewery, so it can brew all year. Much of the work stays by hand: rice soaked in 10 kg lots, a medium-temperature quick starter, a three-stage mash, pressing in a tank press and bottle pasteurisation. Its fourth toji, a woman, took over in 2018.
